$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Cloud Deploy (clouddeploy.googleapis.com v1). See eventarc.json for the contract. Core: core/gcp_clouddeploy_core.py.

gcp.clouddeploy.pipelines_targets.title: Delivery pipelines + targets (serial pipelines, standard and canary strategies, gke and run targets, requireApproval)
limitations: Validated like the real API (exactly one runtime per target, unique stages, canary percentages, targetsPresentCondition for missing targets, force-delete of pipelines with releases). multiTarget, custom/Anthos targets, predeploy/postdeploy hooks, customCanaryDeployment, automations, deploy policies and custom target types are refused or not modelled. LROs complete inline.

gcp.clouddeploy.releases_rollouts.title: Releases + rollouts state machine (render, approve, advance canary phases, retry/ignore/cancel, rollbackTarget, job runs) deploying to the simulator's Cloud Run and GKE
limitations: The deploy job really deploys the release's buildArtifacts image: it updates (or creates) the Cloud Run service (canary phases split traffic between the new and previous revision) or replaces the Deployment in the GKE cluster's data plane (canary phases run a <name>-canary Deployment). The service / Deployment name comes from deployParameters (service, deployment, namespace, container; default = pipeline id).

Skaffold is not run: manifests are not rendered from skaffold.yaml and verify jobs do not execute the verify container (they succeed unless the deployParameter vyomi-verify=fail). One rollout per target is not serialized (no PENDING queue). On Nano the same logic runs against Nano's Cloud Run / GKE state.
